title: Venipuncture / Blood Draw
summary: Collecting a venous blood sample for laboratory analysis.
steps: Review lab orders. Verify patient ID using two identifiers. Explain procedure.
Select site — antecubital fossa preferred. Avoid hematoma sites, edematous areas, mastectomy side.
Apply tourniquet 3–4 inches above site. Palpate and identify vein.
Perform hand hygiene and don gloves.
Clean site with alcohol swab using circular motion. Allow to dry fully (30 seconds).
Anchor vein with non-dominant thumb pulling skin taut below the site.
Insert needle bevel up at 15–30° angle into the vein.
Advance needle slightly after flashback. Attach first collection tube — blood will flow automatically.
Keep needle stable while changing tubes using correct draw order (see below).
Release tourniquet before removing needle (or as last tube fills).
Remove needle swiftly, apply gauze with firm pressure for 2–3 minutes.
Invert tubes gently per manufacturer instructions. Label at bedside.
Apply bandage. Document.
nursing_considerations: Draw order: Blood cultures → Light blue (citrate) → Red/Gold → Green → Purple/Lavender → Grey.
Mix tubes by gentle inversion immediately after collection.
If using a line draw, discard first 5–10mL per facility policy.
Do not draw from an arm with an active IV infusion in the same site if possible.
Apply pressure longer (5 min) for patients on anticoagulants.

title: Clean-Catch Midstream Urine Specimen
summary: Collecting a midstream urine specimen with minimal contamination for urinalysis or culture.
steps: Verify order. Explain procedure to patient. Ideally collect first morning void for best results.
Label the specimen container at bedside before collection.
Instruct or assist patient:
Female: Spread labia with one hand. With the other hand, use 3 towelettes to cleanse: center, then left side, then right side — always front to back. Do not let labia fall back.
Male: Retract foreskin (if present). Cleanse meatus with all 3 towelettes in a circular motion from center outward.
Instruct patient to start urinating into the toilet. After the initial stream (first 2–4 seconds), move the specimen container into the stream mid-void.
Collect 30–60 mL (or fill container approximately half full). Move container away before end of stream.
Cap specimen container immediately without contaminating the inside.
Perform hand hygiene.
Label specimen with patient name, MRN, date, time, and initials.
Place in biohazard bag and transport to lab within 30 minutes, or refrigerate at 4°C if delay is expected.
Document collection time and method.
nursing_considerations: If patient is unable to collect a clean catch, a straight catheter specimen is preferred for culture accuracy.
Contaminated specimens show mixed flora on culture — they often need to be repeated.
Transport specimen to lab within 30 minutes. Refrigerate if unavoidable delay — room temp ≥2 hours invalidates culture.
Do not collect specimen from a diaper, absorbent pad, or bedpan — highly contaminated.
Document any factors that may affect results: recent antibiotic use, menstruation, Foley removal.

title: Wound Culture Collection
summary: Collecting a wound swab or tissue specimen for microbiological analysis of suspected infection.
equipment: Culture swab (Levine technique swab or Culturette)
steps: Verify provider order. Collect culture before initiating or changing antibiotics if possible.
Perform hand hygiene. Don clean gloves.
Remove old dressing and assess the wound.
Irrigate the wound with sterile NS to clean surface exudate — do NOT culture wound surfaces without cleaning first (surface bacteria ≠ causative organisms).
Remove clean gloves. Perform hand hygiene. Don sterile gloves.
Levine technique (preferred): Press the swab firmly into the wound. Rotate the swab 360° using Z-stroke technique over a 1 cm² area of viable tissue. Apply enough pressure to express tissue fluid.
Do NOT swab pus, necrotic tissue, or eschar — these yield contaminated results.
For deep wound/tissue culture (if ordered): use a sterile needle and syringe to aspirate fluid from within the wound depth.
Immediately insert swab into culture transport medium and activate the tube's medium.
Label at bedside: patient name, MRN, wound location, date/time, collection method.
Place in biohazard bag. Transport to lab promptly (within 2 hours for aerobic cultures).
Apply new dressing to wound. Document collection.
nursing_considerations: Always clean the wound before swabbing — swabbing unclean exudate grows surface contaminants, not the infecting organisms.
Levine technique (pressure/rotation) is more reliable than simple swipe — it collects subsurface bacteria.
Anaerobic cultures require specific transport medium — confirm with the lab order.
Notify provider if wound shows systemic signs of infection (fever, elevated WBC) — culture alone does not diagnose infection.
Multiple wound cultures from the same wound site at the same time are usually redundant — one Levine technique swab is typically sufficient.

title: Sputum Specimen Collection
summary: Collecting an expectorated sputum sample for culture, sensitivity, or cytology.
equipment: Mask (for nurse if patient has suspected respiratory infection)
Mouth rinse water (plain water — not mouthwash)
steps: Verify order: culture and sensitivity, AFB smear, cytology, or other testing.
Best timing: first thing in the morning before eating — secretions pool overnight and are most concentrated.
Explain the difference between sputum (from deep in the lungs) and saliva (from the mouth) — patient must cough deeply.
Have patient rinse mouth with plain water to reduce oral flora contamination. Do NOT use mouthwash or toothpaste.
Don gloves and mask. Have patient sit upright.
Instruct patient to take several slow deep breaths, then forcefully cough and expectorate sputum directly into the specimen container.
Goal: ≥1 mL of purulent or mucopurulent sputum. Thin saliva is an inadequate specimen.
If patient cannot produce sputum spontaneously, consider: nebulized hypertonic saline to induce sputum, or chest physiotherapy.
Cap container immediately. Label at bedside.
Place in biohazard bag. Transport to lab promptly — within 1–2 hours for routine culture; AFB specimens may be refrigerated.
Document time of collection, specimen appearance, and patient tolerance.
nursing_considerations: Wear a mask when collecting sputum from patients with suspected TB, COVID, or other airborne organisms.
An inadequate specimen (all saliva, <1 mL) should be recollected — lab may reject it.
For suspected TB: collect 3 consecutive early-morning specimens on 3 separate days for AFB smear and culture.
Induced sputum (hypertonic saline nebulization) yields better specimens for difficult-to-collect patients.
In intubated patients, a suctioned tracheal aspirate is preferred over expectorated sputum.
